summary: H.R. 8646 provides fiscal year 2027 appropriations for the Department of Agriculture, the Food and Drug Administration, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, related agencies, and domestic and international food assistance programs. It sets funding levels and establishes rules for agricultural research, farm loans, rural infrastructure, food safety inspections, and nutrition programs.

affected_groups.effect: Receive access to direct and guaranteed farm ownership, operating, and emergency loans, crop insurance funding, and agricultural research support.
Affected by funding allocations and rules for domestic food assistance programs such as SNAP, WIC, and school lunch programs.
Benefit from loans and grants for rural housing, community facilities, water and waste disposal systems, electrification, and broadband expansion.
Subject to FDA oversight, inspections, user fees, and updated statutory standards regarding animal food and labeling claims.

key_provisions: Provides annual appropriations for USDA agencies, agricultural research, farm production and conservation programs, and rural development initiatives.

Allocates specific funding for domestic food programs, including child nutrition programs, the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), and the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC).
Provides funding for the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) supported in part by various user fees, and sets requirements for animal food regulation under the PURR Act.
Finances foreign food assistance programs, including Food for Peace Title II grants and McGovern-Dole International Food for Education grants.
Imposes restrictions on certain regulatory actions, such as rules concerning poultry grower contracting, and sets rules for domestic sourcing of iron and steel in rural water projects.
Provides liability protections for individuals and nonprofit organizations that donate apparently fit pet-related products in good faith.
